brief: Goldman's Privorotsky frames the tape as narrow. Mag7 leadership stays extremely concentrated while Russell and most of Asia lag fresh US highs, which he reads less as generic risk-off and more as higher oil and higher real rates biting duration-sensitive assets. European flows were heavily for sale into the rally despite OAT and oil relief, leaving the flow picture unconstructive. In AI, Samsung's Q3 prelim, SpaceX's reported $40bn raise to buy Nvidia chips, Marvell's guidance (bullish for Broadcom), and Mistral's new open-weight model all support compute demand, though added AI-ecosystem leverage worries the market. He stays constructive on AI fundamentals. Middle East conflict is broadening (Houthi/Saudi strikes) even as physical oil flows improve, per Vitol, making it more a logistics problem than a barrels problem. Iran may be drifting toward frozen conflict. RBI hiked 25bp. Fed October hike odds sit near 20% versus about 85% for December, yet the 10yr holds near 5.30%. Le Pen's new savings plan eased near-term OAT tail risk, but her EU-contribution cap creates a medium-term euro risk instead. He stays bearish on bonds, Russell, and Europe absent an energy fix, wanting rate relief, despite low positioning being a tailwind.
